$comment: LB-Web-5. Marketplace fee comparison data for the /who-we-are page (LB-Web-6). Every rate here is from the platform's own published fee schedule where one exists; where a platform does not publish a fixed rate (Groupon) that is recorded as a range with its source. Rates are decimals (0.065 = 6.5%). Do NOT hardcode computed totals in the UI - use the fee_components so a rate change here flows through to the charts.

meta.notes: Fees change often. Re-check the source_url on each platform before quoting these publicly. Percentages are expressed as decimals.

lytebuy.name: lytebuy

fee_components.label: Commission
fee_components.notes: 4% of the item subtotal, deducted from the vendor payout. NOT charged on shipping, unlike Etsy, eBay and Amazon which all take their cut of the shipping too. Per-vendor overridable (Vendor.commission_rate_bps); pilot vendors are set to 0.

fee_components.label: Buyer service fee
fee_components.notes: Charged to the BUYER at checkout as a separate 'Service fee' line, on top of the item price. It is not deducted from the vendor payout, so it does not belong in a seller-cost comparison - see honest_caveats.

fee_components.label: Bank transfer fee
fee_components.notes: 1% of each withdrawal to the vendor bank account, capped at $25. Charged per WITHDRAWAL, not per sale, so a vendor who withdraws monthly pays it monthly.

seller_pays.payment_processing_note: The vendor absorbs Stripe's processing fee (2.9% + $0.30), the same as on every other platform in this comparison. See docs/PAYMENT_SPLIT.md.
seller_pays.sales_tax_note: lytebuy is the marketplace facilitator: it calculates, collects and remits sales tax. Tax is a pass-through liability, not part of the vendor payout, and there is no third-party tax-engine fee (rates come from a free public table, not Stripe Tax at 0.5%/txn).

vouchers.notes: Vouchers carry the same 4% as any other checkout - there is no separate voucher rate.

lytebuy.verified: Confirmed against the codebase, not marketing copy: fee mechanics in lytebuy-backend/app/services/fees.py and ledger.py.

platforms.name: Etsy

fee_components.label: Listing fee
fee_components.notes: Per listing, renewed every 4 months or on each sale.

fee_components.label: Transaction fee
fee_components.notes: 6.5% of the total the buyer pays, INCLUDING shipping and gift wrap.

fee_components.label: Payment processing
fee_components.notes: US rate. Charged by Etsy Payments on top of the transaction fee.

optional_costs.label: Offsite Ads
optional_costs.notes: 15% under $10k trailing-12-month sales, 12% at or above. Becomes MANDATORY and permanently un-opt-out-able once the shop passes $10k. Only charged when an offsite ad leads to the sale.

platforms.effective_rate_note: Mandatory fees (listing + 6.5% + 3% + $0.25) work out at about 9.7-14% of the order, highest on small orders where the flat $0.20 and $0.25 bite hardest: 14.0% on a $10 order, 10.8% on $35, 9.7% on $262. Widely-quoted '11-15%' figures are close but do not hold at the top of the range without Offsite Ads. With 15% Offsite Ads the total lands at roughly 25-29%.
platforms.effective_rate_verified: Computed from the fee_components above; reproduces Etsy's own published example of $3.78 on a $30 item with $5 shipping exactly.
platforms.source_note: etsy.com returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches; figures cross-checked across multiple current 2026 fee guides rather than read from the source page directly.

platforms.name: eBay

fee_components.label: Final value fee
fee_components.notes: 13.6% for most categories on the total sale INCLUDING shipping and sales tax; drops to 2.35% on the portion above $7,500 per item. Category-dependent.

fee_components.label: Per-order fee
fee_components.notes: $0.30 on orders of $10 or less, $0.40 above.

optional_costs.label: Insertion fee
optional_costs.notes: First 250 listings a month are free.

platforms.effective_rate_note: The 13.6% headline understates it: with the per-order fee the effective rate is 13.8-16.6% (16.6% on a $10 order, 14.7% on $35, 13.8% on $262), and it is charged on shipping and sales tax as well as the item.
platforms.source_note: Read directly from eBay's seller centre.

platforms.name: Groupon

fee_components.label: Commission on redeemed vouchers
fee_components.notes: Groupon publishes NO fixed rate - it is negotiated per merchant before launch and varies by industry, discount and deal structure. The 20/30/40% range is taken from the worked examples on Groupon's own merchant pricing page ($50 voucher nets the merchant $40 / $35 / $30).

additional_costs.label: Buyer-facing discount
additional_costs.notes: The commission sits ON TOP of the discount the merchant already gives the buyer to run the deal. This is the real cost of a Groupon campaign and is why the effective take is far higher than the commission alone.

myths: The widely repeated '50% discount plus 50% commission' figure is called a myth on Groupon's own pricing page. Do not publish it as fact.

payout_terms.notes: The merchant is paid only when a voucher is REDEEMED, not when it is sold. Unredeemed vouchers are refunded to the customer and the merchant is not billed - but nor is it paid. Payouts run weekly on Wednesdays, ACH landing 3-5 business days later.
payout_terms.cash_flow_note: This is a genuine working-capital difference vs lytebuy, where the vendor is paid out on the sale rather than waiting on redemption.

platforms.effective_rate_note: 20-40% of voucher face value, negotiated, and charged on top of the promotional discount the merchant funds.
platforms.source_note: Read directly from Groupon's merchant pricing page. Their SEC 10-Q filings do not break out a gross-billings-to-revenue take rate, so no derived figure is claimed here.

platforms.name: Amazon Handmade

fee_components.label: Referral fee
fee_components.notes: 15% on all products, no minimum referral fee.

platforms.effective_rate_note: A flat 15%, with no listing fee and no separate payment-processing fee.

platforms.name: Faire
platforms.comparable_note: Wholesale (brand to retailer), not retail. Included for context on what independent makers pay elsewhere, not as a like-for-like checkout comparison.

fee_components.label: Commission, first order from a Faire-sourced retailer
fee_components.notes: 15% ongoing commission plus a one-time 10% referral fee.

platforms.name: Shopify
platforms.comparable_note: A storefront the vendor rents and must drive their own traffic to, not a marketplace with built-in demand. Its low per-order rate comes with a monthly subscription and no discovery.

fee_components.label: Extra fee for not using Shopify Payments

stripe.name: Stripe
stripe.note: Not a competitor - the processor underneath lytebuy and most platforms here. Included so the charts can show processing cost consistently, since it is a real cost on EVERY row including lytebuy's.
stripe.stripe_tax_note: lytebuy does NOT pay this - tax rates come from a free public table, so there is no per-transaction tax-engine fee.

honest_caveats: lytebuy charges the VENDOR a 4% commission (config PLATFORM/VENDOR_COMMISSION_BPS=400) and separately charges the BUYER a 4% service fee at checkout. Only the commission belongs in a seller-cost chart; including the buyer fee would double-count and overstate what a vendor pays. The vendor also pays 1% capped at $25 to withdraw (bank transfer fee) and 1.2% on in-person card charges.
The vendor absorbs the Stripe processing fee on lytebuy, exactly as sellers do on Etsy, eBay and Shopify. Do not present lytebuy as covering it - the codebase says otherwise (docs/PAYMENT_SPLIT.md).
Groupon has no published rate. Present it as a 20-40% range from their own worked examples, never as a single number, and never repeat the '50%' folklore their pricing page explicitly calls a myth.

Shopify and Faire are not like-for-like: Shopify is a rented storefront with no built-in demand, Faire is wholesale. Both are flagged comparable_to_lytebuy: false. Charting them as direct rivals would be misleading.

Etsy's headline 6.5% is not the real cost - the listing fee, 3% + $0.25 processing and possibly-mandatory 15% Offsite Ads are what take it to 11-15%+. The comparison should use the effective rate, not the headline.

The genuine lytebuy advantages that are NOT just the percentage: sales tax is calculated, collected and remitted by the platform at no per-transaction tax-engine cost, and voucher vendors are paid on the sale rather than waiting for redemption as they do on Groupon.
